chunks: Ali, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Muawiya Bin Ammar, who said:
Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) said: The one in Ihram must not look into the mirror for adornment; so if he looks, he should recite the Talbiyya.

key_terms.الْمُحْرِمُ: The person in the state of Ihram

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for a person in Ihram who looks in the mirror for adornment?
ai.summary: This ruling from al-Kafi highlights the preservation of humility and detachment from worldly vanity during the sacred state of Ihram, a core principle in Shia jurisprudence. The requirement to recite the Talbiyya upon looking serves as a spiritual reset, reorienting the pilgrim’s focus from self-adornment to the remembrance of God. This practice underscores the theological emphasis on inner purity mirroring the external state of consecration.

en.hubeali: Ali, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Muawiya Bin Ammar who said,
‘Abu Abdullahasws said: ‘The one in Ihraam cannot look into the mirror in order to adorn. So if he looks, he should exclaim Talbiyya’.
en.sarwar: 2. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Mu‘awiyah ibn ‘Ammar who has said the following: “
Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘One in the state of Ihram must not look into the mirror; if one does so, one must say the Talbiyah (here I am, O Lord, to obey Your command).”’
